Riley Thomson: morning team, day 1 issue. i connected via Okta and VPN shows connected, but i can't reach our internal pgadmin UI at pgadmin.internal.redwood:9090. browser times out. can anyone point me to the usual onboarding checks?

Nora Patel: welcome! first things first: can you ping the ip if you have it? sometimes DNS points to a different host on home networks. also which VPN client (Okta Tunnel / WireGuard)?

Riley Thomson: Okta Tunnel on macbook. i don't have a hostname resolved to a corp ip - `dig pgadmin.internal.redwood` returns 192.168.1.45 (my local IoT). weird.

Kai Morgan: that looks like CIDR overlap / DNS bleed. corporate IPv4s are in 172.18.0.0/16 for prod infra. If your home uses 192.168.1.0/24 that's odd the lookup returns your local device. run `scutil --dns` and `ip route` and paste outputs.

Riley Thomson: scutil shows search domain internal.redwood but resolver returns local IP. ip route shows default via 192.168.1.1 and 172.18.0.0/16 via 172.20.4.1 dev tun0.

IT Support: two things happen often: 1) if the local LAN has a host named pgadmin (some routers advertise local mDNS/NetBIOS) it may shadow the internal DNS when short names are used. 2) split-tunnel DNS can be quirky: search domain present but mDNS and hosts file may resolve locally first. Try `ping -c1 pgadmin.internal.redwood` and `dig +short pgadmin.internal.redwood @172.20.4.2` (corporate DNS) to confirm.

Riley Thomson: `dig +short pgadmin.internal.redwood @172.20.4.2` returns 172.18.5.20 (corp ip). `ping` still hits 192.168.1.45. so local resolver is preferring local hostname before the enterprise DNS answer.

Kai Morgan: ok. quick workarounds: 1) use the corp IP directly: `https://172.18.5.20:9090` (ok if cert matches IP or use host header), 2) add an /etc/hosts entry mapping pgadmin.internal.redwood -> 172.18.5.20, or 3) disable mDNS/NetBIOS on your router (not ideal). We'll also check whether the VPN pushed DNS properly.

Riley Thomson: i tried https to the IP and TLS fails because cert CN is pgadmin.internal.redwood so browser blocks it. host entry would fix that. is editing /etc/hosts allowed on company policy for personal devices?

IT Support: it's allowed for temporary debugging but note it's persistent. For managed devices we push a host file via Intune; for personal devices OK to add host entry for now. also you can add `--insecure` for curl but avoid that for browsers.

Riley Thomson: added `172.18.5.20 pgadmin.internal.redwood` to /etc/hosts and browser loads UI. however when i try to connect to the DB from my local psql client it times out on port 5432. gui loads but DB connection fails.

Nora Patel: GUI might be on a bastion-proxied endpoint (http(s) front end), but direct DB port likely blocked to your session. New-hires often need their Okta device group added to the DB security group or use an SSH tunnel via bastion. Can you access bastion? `ssh ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal`

Riley Thomson: ssh times out. `dig bastion.redwood.internal @172.20.4.2` gives 172.18.200.5. `ssh ubuntu@172.18.200.5` also times out.

Kai Morgan: that suggests your device isn't allowed by the bastion SG or the SG only allows certain egress ranges. What's your public IP (from https://ifconfig.me) and are you on a home ISP?

Riley Thomson: my public IP is 203.0.113.78 (home ISP).

infra-bot: Created INFRA-5123: "New-hire bastion access for Riley Thomson (203.0.113.78)".

IT Support: looking at the onboarding ticket, your Okta device group is `new-hires-sfo` but it wasn't yet mapped to the bastion allowlist due to a timing gap. I've added the public IP group rule and pushed a change to the bastion SG. Please disconnect and reconnect the VPN to pick it up.

okta-bot: User Riley Thomson (riley.thomson@redwood.com) authenticated via Okta at 2026-01-22T09:15:12Z

Riley Thomson: reconnected. `ssh ubuntu@172.18.200.5` now connects. thanks. trying to open local tunnel: `ssh -L 5433:10.10.5.20:5432 ubuntu@172.18.200.5` then `psql -h localhost -p 5433` gives `could not connect to server: Connection refused`.

Nora Patel: double-check the target IP inside corp (10.10.5.20) 10.10.* is our private app network and some DB hosts are only accessible from specific subnets. Can you ssh into bastion and then `nc -vz 10.10.5.20 5432` from the bastion host to verify reachability?

Riley Thomson: on bastion `nc -vz 10.10.5.20 5432` returns `Connection timed out`. so the DB itself blocks direct connections from bastion. likely DB is in a private cluster that only accepts connections from the app tier or a specific jump host.

Kai Morgan: ok that's by design for prod. For dev access we provide a jump proxy host `db-jump.internal.redwood` that is in the DB SG. Try `ssh -L 5433:10.10.5.20:5432 ubuntu@db-jump.internal.redwood` (you may need to be added to db-access okta group).

IT Support: I added you to `db-access-dev` Okta group and created INFRA-5124 to ensure db-jump mapping includes new-hires. Rolling policy now.

infra-bot: INFRA-5124 created: "Map db-jump allowlist to db-access-dev group".

Riley Thomson: after reconnecting `ssh -L 5433:10.10.5.20:5432 ubuntu@db-jump.internal.redwood` works and `psql -h localhost -p 5433` connects. thanks!

SRE Oncall: adding a note for onboarding runbook: 1) short hostnames can resolve to local LAN devices; prefer FQDNs or add host entries when onboarding; 2) ensure new-hires Okta groups are added to bastion and db-jump SGs on day 0 to avoid timing gaps; 3) document the db-jump pattern for dev DB access.

Riley Thomson: all good now. will add a checklist note to my onboarding doc: "Reconnect VPN after SG changes, add host entry for problematic hostnames, use db-jump for DB access." thanks everyone :heart:
